summary: Candidates tell the press how many doors they have knocked, as the mark of effort.
realLife: A candidate who had knocked about three thousand doors told the paper residents felt ignored on traffic and a golf course plan.
sources: New Bedford Light, Shawn Oliver: residents feel ignored on traffic jams, golf course plans and other issues: https://newbedfordlight.org/shawn-oliver-residents-feel-ignored-on-traffic-jams-golf-course-plans-and-other-issues/
inGame: campaign day choices (canvass shift) and the campaign's own records; no count is said in speech by rule

turns.turn: The paper prints no door count and says the candidate barely campaigned
The count is large but residents still say they are ignored
